sections.markdown:
## C — Insurance and financial responsibility: required liability limits, proof of insurance, NV LIVE lapses, crash reporting and SR-22, what to do in a crash, and the driving record with demerit points
Knowledge domain: the liability insurance every Nevada vehicle must carry and how proof is shown, what happens when coverage lapses, when and how a crash must be reported, what an SR-22 is, the steps to take at a crash scene, how long violations stay on a driving record, and how demerit points lead to suspension.

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
All Nevada motorists must comply with mandatory insurance and financial responsibility laws, and every registered motor vehicle in the state must be covered by liability insurance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
Keep the insurer's Evidence of Insurance Card in the vehicle, or have it ready in electronic form to show on a mobile device. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
Nevada's minimum liability coverage is $25,000 for injury or death of one person in a crash and $50,000 for injury or death of two or more people in one crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
Nevada's minimum liability coverage also includes $20,000 for damage to or destruction of other people's property in any one crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
NV LIVE, the Nevada Liability Insurance Validation Electronically program, works with licensed insurers to flag registrations whose insurance has ended or lapsed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
If a registration is suspended for an insurance lapse with no replacement coverage for that period, you pay a reinstatement fee plus fines starting at $250 and reaching up to $1,750 for each vehicle on that policy. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
Further penalties for an insurance lapse can include an SR-22 requirement, a 30-day driver license suspension, or both. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A01
When law enforcement investigates a crash, the officer sends your insurance information and a description of the damage or injuries to the DMV. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A01
If police do not investigate a crash that causes $750 or more in damage or injures anyone, you must send a Report of Crash Form, the SR-1, to the DMV within 10 days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A01
The SR-1 must be completed by anyone who was the driver or the registered owner of a vehicle in the crash, and the form is available at DMV offices, the Nevada Highway Patrol, local police and the DMV website. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A02
After a crash, the DMV Financial Responsibility Section decides who was at fault, whether every vehicle and driver was insured, and the total liability. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A02
An at-fault driver without liability insurance may have the license or registration suspended, must post a deposit with the DMV to cover crash costs, or must arrange payment with the other parties. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A02
Failing to report a crash to the DMV can lead to suspension of your driver license, your vehicle registration, or both. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A02
An SR-22 is liability insurance on a driver license that lets the DMV monitor the insurance of a suspended or revoked driver through reports from the insurer, and it may be required for reinstatement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A02
SR-22 coverage starts when you actually reinstate, you file the form only once, and you should not buy it until every other reinstatement requirement is met. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A02
At a crash, stop, get medical help for anyone injured, warn traffic and notify law enforcement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A02
In a fender bender with only property damage and no injuries, move the vehicle if it can be moved safely to a spot that does not block traffic, then return to the scene. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A02
Exchange your name, address, driver license number, registration and insurance information with every other driver involved. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A02
If you hit an unattended vehicle or other property, give the owner your name, address, license number, registration and insurance details, in person or in a note left behind. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A03
A Nevada driver license is a privilege, and it can be suspended, revoked or canceled if you stop driving safely and obeying the rules. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A03
Crashes and traffic convictions go on your driving record, including violations committed in other states. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A03
Most violations can be reported to your insurer for three years, while convictions related to driving under the influence stay on the record for seven years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A03
Every traffic violation carries demerit points, added once a court sends the DMV notice of a conviction or civil infraction, and points are counted over a 12-month period. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A03
Receiving 12 or more demerit points in any 12-month period means your license will be suspended. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A03
With 3 to 11 points, completing a DMV-approved traffic safety course removes up to 3 points, but only once in any 12-month period, and the conviction itself stays in your driving history. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A03
A conviction for a major offense such as DUI or causing substantial bodily harm revokes the license; these offenses carry no demerit points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A04
Demerit points: reckless driving is 8 points, and careless driving or failing to give information or render aid at a crash scene is 6 points. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A04
Demerit points: following too closely, failing to yield the right-of-way, failing to yield to a pedestrian, and disobeying a traffic signal or stop sign are 4 points each. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A04
Demerit points: impeding traffic or driving too slowly, failing to dim headlights, and a prima facie speed violation or driving too fast for conditions are 2 points each. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A04
Speeding points rise with speed over the limit: 1 to 10 mph over is 1 point, 11 to 20 is 2 points, 21 to 30 is 3 points, 31 to 40 is 4 points, and 41 mph or more is 5 points. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A04
It is illegal to give false information on a Nevada license application, to alter your license, to lend it to anyone, or to use another person's license. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0078]

Misconceptions: carrying insurance is not enough, proof must be in the vehicle or on your phone; a police-investigated crash still reaches the DMV through the officer's report; traffic school does not erase the conviction, only up to three points; DUI is not a points offense, it brings revocation; out-of-state tickets do count on a Nevada record.
Mnemonics: twenty-five, fifty, twenty for liability; seven fifty and ten days for the SR-1; twelve points in twelve months means suspension; traffic school takes three, once a year; reckless eight, careless six.
Glossary: liability insurance means coverage that pays for injury or damage you cause others; SR-1 means the Report of Crash Form; SR-22 means DMV-monitored proof of liability insurance for reinstatement; demerit point means a value added to your record for each violation; revocation means cancellation of the license as opposed to a temporary suspension.
Dynamic facts: minimum coverage amounts, lapse fines, the reporting threshold and the point schedule are set by law and can change, and the DMV mailing address, phone and email contacts change too, so confirm them on the DMV website.
